title: Design a GPU-Aware ML CI/CD Platform
prompt: Design CI/CD for GPU-dependent ML services. It must build native extensions safely, run compatibility and benchmark gates on appropriate accelerators, publish immutable artifacts, deploy by digest, and recover from GPU worker failures. Explain how this differs from a general workflow engine.

response.placeholder: Trace an immutable artifact from source commit through ABI checks, GPU benchmarks, and a digest-pinned rollout.
response.reference_answer:
## Distinct scope
This is not a clone of a generic linear workflow service: it specializes the artifact and execution contracts for GPU/ABI compatibility and model-serving benchmark gates. It can run on top of a general workflow scheduler such as the linear CI/CD engine.

## Artifact path
Pin source and dependency lockfiles, build an ABI-tagged wheel or container, attach CUDA/driver/framework compatibility metadata, scan/sign it, and store every output by content digest. A manifest links source commit, compiler/toolchain, dependency ABI, model version, and benchmark data version.

## GPU execution and gates
Lease compatible GPUs with heartbeats and fencing; use warm pools for short tests and exclusive leases for training-like jobs. Run deterministic smoke tests, compatibility matrix tests, latency/throughput/quality benchmark gates, and detect regressions against a pinned baseline. GPU partitioning such as MIG is acceptable only when workload isolation and memory behavior are validated.

## Deploy and rollback
Promote immutable digests through staged environments, gate on runtime health and model metrics, and roll back by digest. The event log makes terminal promotion idempotent and auditable.

## Progressive Hints
1. A package name is not an immutable artifact.
2. GPU compatibility is more than a CUDA version string.
3. Benchmark inputs must be versioned too.
